data.turoyo: Bann 1975 b ʕAnqara i ḥkume kdəršo u šəwolo daw waqfat daʕ ʕitawoṯo. Xori ʕAziz kḥoḏ̣ər harke w kšore (!) u qaṭro.

rationale: Author-marked knot metaphor recurs with plural qatre at Jan 4.II/823. Searches qaṭro and qatre found no existing item; keep under round 1 figurative 1b, not another solve sense. Supplied machine English.

summary: All 90 supplied records received decisions. Repeated tokens in a verse are counted as tokens, not independent semantic evidence; page citations in Prym–Socin, LuF and Talay are not replaced by text-number citations without an edition concordance.

The two independent abstract-object contexts support 1b; the three b-iḏ- occurrences in JTM 5.1 support construction 2 with a person coded as possessor of iḏ-. Their exact active/Detransitive morphology needs checking; the published label is provisional Infectum, not a newly invented Detransitive box.

Concrete patients can be zero-marked or l-marked (105/52); agents can be l-marked (PrS 73/98). Bound patient forms and discourse are needed to disambiguate šralle. ruḥe supplies an overt reflexive object in the active construction.

Detransitive forms denote spontaneous detachment, regained freedom or a background result state. Existing unnumbered examples retain their wording and acquire only an explicit Detransitive sense 1 gloss. The girls’ command/result pair gives one new Imperativ attestation.

Stem II begin is already attested at 37/14 followed by kṯuli, another Preterit. The alleged extra editorial-note example is already stored as a note in this input, not as a second example, so no structural correction is needed.

At LuF 3/52, kul yawmo supplies habituality for Infectum-wa; the cattle-release example adds a 1sg.f form. At Talay 1/157, the quoted active ko-Preterit is projected into a future report, so completed perspective is distinct from narrative time.

PrS 80/69 has an observable translation mismatch even though no alignment flag was supplied. It is excluded from additions. Duplicate existing passages at LuF 2/10, PrS 67/67, 37/14, 65/407, Talay 1/63 and Talay 1/179 are not copied.
All 17 tokens reviewed; the two šurewo tokens share one example. Round 1 fills ordinary I Infectum and Imperativ cells, but II Preterit remains thin and II Infectum has no example.
II mšareli begins interviews, community work, publishing and writing, with b- nouns or d- clauses. III mašre is a separate causative stem and is not inferred from mšare-.

Explicit Classical Syriac šari begin and quoted šreno bex dwell are foreign-register comparisons. Neither establishes an ordinary Turoyo form; in particular the latter cannot justify a new dwelling sense under this loosening root.

New I Detransitive figurative 1b is separate from active 1b. In Jan 4.0/19 the patient question, not the solver, controls the clause; its negative condition remains suspended in the supplied source. No missing continuation is supplied.
All new English examples retain the project machine text. Existing senses, including inherited English begin and mixed transitive/intransitive wording, are not rewritten.
Confirm the segmentation and stem/diathesis of mašəryowa in Bilgic Die Rolle Məḏyaḏs im Tur Abdin/8 and the gender switch between šərenawola and šərenawole.
Are šširoyo / ššəryo in JTM 5.1 forms of this root, and how are their onset and endings segmented? Is b-iḏ- success a conventional construction?
Does šuranwo ḥaṣayye mean relaxing, feeling safe or leaving the rear unguarded at JTM 3.2/12?
Does MAC Besim Martyrdom of Maferyono/5 concern canonical dispensation or dissolution of the spiritual relationship itself? Its interrupted syntax does not settle the distinction.
Is šorən in MAC NE Farrucke/7 from šry or šḏy, and what does the cotton-bow NP code?
Confirm Detransitive Imperativ Məšrewu versus active III Imperativ at MAC NE Mor Barsaumo/48; the subsequent šarən favors addressing the freed daughters.
The German at PrS 80/69 translates a different action. Supply the aligned German before using this unwrapping example.
Can an edition concordance verify PrS 17/35 versus prs 40/7 and prs 181/6? Similar wording alone is insufficient to replace those older references.
Jan 2.12/3212: does šuranwo i ḥalyuṯo mean release sweetness into the liquid or lose their sweetness? No technical extraction sense is proposed without that distinction.
Jan 4.0/19: obtain the rest of the sentence and verify the force of d lə məšre. The Detransitive problem-solving use is clear, but until in the machine English is interpretive.
Jan 3.17/317: supply the continuation after mu ḥarf to identify the written starting point; no missing text has been reconstructed.
Jan 2.12/2833 šreno bex: this is quoted Classical Syriac dwelling. Confirm whether editors want a separate learned-homonym cross-reference; no Turoyo dwelling proposal is made.

Release from magical immobilization and release of an engagement or spiritual-kinship relationship extend the kinds of bond or restraint; no separate magical or ecclesiastical technical sense is established.

šuranwo ḥaṣayye occurs where a front is reported safe. A security/relaxation interpretation is contextual; leaving the rear unguarded remains possible. Distinguish this from literal belt loosening and from losing contact with one’s tent.
Hedgehog self-release uses an active reflexive ruḥe; raisins as subject release or lose sweetness. These participant extensions do not themselves establish uncurl or extraction senses.

Administrative settlement, figurative knots and untying historical roots support round 1 abstract-solving 1b in modern discussion. The roots context also includes uncover/reveal verbs, so its exact metaphor is descriptive rather than a new sense.
